strategy.why_this_method: The integrand is a product where differentiating x simplifies it and integrating e to the x leaves the same form.
strategy.alternatives: Substitution does not simplify the product because neither factor is the derivative of the other.

steps.title: Choose the parts
steps.explanation: Choose the algebraic factor as u because its derivative becomes simpler. The exponential factor is easy to integrate.
steps.common_mistake: Choosing u = e^x does not reduce the remaining integral.

steps.title: Differentiate and integrate the chosen parts
steps.explanation: Differentiate u and integrate dv. These are the pieces needed in the parts formula.

steps.title: Apply the integration-by-parts formula
steps.explanation: Use the formula integral u dv equals uv minus integral v du. The remaining integral is now elementary.
steps.common_mistake: The formula has a minus sign before the remaining integral.

steps.title: Evaluate the remaining integral
steps.explanation: The antiderivative of e to the x is itself. Add the arbitrary constant because this is an indefinite integral.
steps.common_mistake: Do not omit the constant of integration.

final_answer.plain: The antiderivative is e to the x times x minus 1, plus C.

check.detail: The product rule gives e^x(x - 1) + e^x = x e^x.

hints: Differentiate the factor that becomes simpler.
Use integration by parts with u = x.
With u = x and dv = e^x dx, the first term is x e^x.
